name: The Trinity
path: Theology Proper: The Doctrine of God

objectives.text: Identify the one true God as the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit
State the church's confession that there is one God in three persons
Retell the account of Jesus' baptism and identify what the Father, the Son, and the Spirit each do in it
Identify the names of the three persons in the baptism command and in the apostolic benediction
Describe the biblical pattern of praying to the Father in the name of the Son by the help of the Spirit and use it to compose a short class prayer
Explain the Shield of the Trinity diagram to show that each person is God and that the persons are distinct from one another
Identify Bible passages that show the Son and the Holy Spirit are fully God
Explain from Scripture why the three persons are not three gods
Analyze common analogies for the Trinity such as water, an egg, or a shamrock and explain how each one misrepresents the doctrine
Explain how the eternal love among the Father, the Son, and the Spirit shows that God's love did not begin with or depend on creation
Distinguish the personal properties of the Father who begets, the Son who is begotten, and the Spirit who proceeds
Analyze how the persons are equal in power and glory while the Son humbly submits to the Father in his saving mission
Trace the distinct work of the Father, the Son, and the Spirit in redemption through Ephesians 1
Explain the historical setting of the Council of Nicaea and the meaning of the claim that the Son is of one substance with the Father
Interpret the Athanasian Creed's rule that the church neither confuses the persons nor divides the one divine substance
Compare modalism, Arianism, and tritheism with the orthodox doctrine and identify the Scripture each error contradicts
Construct an argument from Old Testament passages that anticipate plurality within the one God while explaining how progressive revelation shapes their reading
Analyze how Trinitarian doctrine shapes elements of Reformed worship such as baptism, the benediction, and the doxology
Evaluate the filioque controversy between Eastern and Western churches using the biblical texts on the sending of the Spirit
Evaluate Unitarian, Jehovah's Witness, and Latter-day Saint teachings about God against Scripture and the Reformed confessions
Explain the doctrine of inseparable operations that the three persons act together in every outward work while each acts in his own proper manner
Evaluate claims that the Trinity is a model for human relationships by weighing the texts offered against the tradition's teaching on divine simplicity and the Creator and creature distinction

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (persons, unity, baptism of Jesus, prayer pattern, Shield, tritheism, analogies, eternal love, roles, redemption, Athanasian Creed, modalism, Old Testament case, filioque, cults, social Trinity). Turned the analogy item into an analysis task, and recast the social Trinity reflection as a critical evaluation in line with Reformed caution about it. Reframed economic subordination as equality of being alongside the Son's submission in his mission. Added objectives on the Trinitarian baptism formula and benediction, the deity of the Son and Spirit, personal properties (begetting and procession), Nicaea and homoousios, Arianism alongside modalism, Trinitarian worship, and inseparable operations. Dropped 1 John 5:7 as textually disputed and 1 Corinthians 11:3 as not central. Replaced unnumbered creed citations with numbered Westminster, Heidelberg, and Belgic references.
